basis: The Lutheran churches are alive today. The Lutheran World Federation's 2023 membership table lists 150 member churches and 78.4 million members. A Pew report of 2011 also names Lutherans as one of the largest Protestant families. The tree has no Lutheran entry between 1906 and today.

evidence.title: Global Christianity: A Report on the Size and Distribution of the World's Christian Population
evidence.quote: the largest distinct denominational families are Anglican (about 11% of the broad Protestant category), Lutheran (about 10%), Baptist (9%) and Reformed/Presbyterian (7%)

basis: The Reformed and Presbyterian churches are alive today. The World Communion of Reformed Churches published its December 2023 newsletter and planned a General Council for October 2025. A Pew report of 2011 counts Reformed and Presbyterian churches among the largest Protestant families. The tree has no Reformed entry after 1906.

The tradition reaches today through the Mennonites and Amish and the Hutterite Brethren. The entry's own text says Mennonites, Amish and Hutterites descend from it. The Hutterite entry holds dated present-day evidence. The tree has no Mennonite or Amish entry after 1890.

evidence.title: Scotland's Census 2022: ethnic group, national identity, language and religion
evidence.quote: ‘Church of Scotland’ remained the largest group among those who said they had a religion.

basis: The Church of Scotland is alive today. Its trustees' report for 2024 describes its work across Scotland. The 2022 national count, published in 2024, names it the largest religious group in Scotland. The tree has no Scottish church entry after 1650.

evidence.title: Actes du 11è Synode national, Noisy-le-Grand
evidence.quote: 11è Synode national de l’Église protestante unie de France Noisy-le-Grand du 18 au 21 mai 2023

basis: The tradition lives on in France in the united Protestant church. That church held its national synod in May 2023, and its own record is the only dated source found. The entry's own text names that church as the heir. The tree has no French Reformed entry after 1787.

presentBody: Catholic Church in England and Wales

evidence.title: Statistics 2023
evidence.publisher: Catholic Bishops' Conference of England and Wales
evidence.quote: On this page, you will find key statistics relating to the life of the Church in England and Wales for 2023.

basis: English Catholicism is alive today. The Bishops' Conference of England and Wales published its statistics for 2023. That is the only dated source found, and it comes from the church itself. The entry's own text says the community continued unbroken. The tree has no entry for it after 1650.

Its carriers ended as a movement. The entry's own text says Puritanism did not survive as a church of its own. English Congregationalism, Presbyterianism and much of the Baptist tradition came out of it, and the tree tells them elsewhere.
endQuote: Puritanism did not survive as a church of its own

tradition: Dutch Further Reformation and refuge culture
basis: Its ideas outlived it, but the entry names no community that continued. Its books travelled and fed German Pietism. The refuge culture left a habit of private toleration and a printing trade.
openQuestion: Some Dutch church bodies today claim the Further Reformation heritage, but the entry's text names no continuing body.

presentBody: Chiesa evangelica valdese, Unione delle chiese metodiste e valdesi

evidence.title: Atti del Sinodo 2024

evidence.title: Il Papa alle Chiese metodiste e valdesi
evidence.quote: Al via domenica 22 agosto a Torre Pellice

basis: The Waldensian Church is alive today. Its synod met at Torre Pellice on 25 to 30 August 2024, and its own record says so. Vatican News reported the synod of August 2021 in the same place. The tree has no Waldensian entry after 1655.

evidence.title: The Society of Jesus in Numbers, 2022 edition
evidence.quote: As of 1 January, 2022, there were 14,439 Jesuits in the world.

evidence.title: Pope Francis: halving of Jesuit numbers worldwide is a lesson in humility
evidence.quote: When I entered the novitiate, we were 33,000 Jesuits. How many are there now? More or less half

basis: The Society of Jesus is alive today. The Jesuits' own 2022 figures count 14,439 members. A news report of December 2021 carries the pope's remark that the order has about half the members it had in the 1960s. The tree has no Jesuit entry after 1650.

tradition: Tridentine parish life in the Catholic Church
presentBody: Catholic parishes, including the Archdiocese of Milan
basis: An episode of a living tradition. The Catholic parish it shaped is alive today, carried by the post-Vatican II parish entry. The entry's own text says the Milan parish lasted into the twentieth century and the diocese still keeps the Ambrosian rite.

tradition: Mission-born Christianities of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries (a group of four regional churches)
basis: The entry names four regional churches and makes no finding on the group. Each has its own entry, and those entries carry the tradition to today. The entry's own text says several of these churches were never broken.
openQuestion: This is a label entry for four churches, so it is living only through its four regional entries.

presentBody: Catholic dioceses of the old Kongo region
descentBasis: A church in the old Kongo region is said to descend from the kingdom of Kongo, but no text in the tree covers 1650 to today.
basis: The Christian church of the old Kongo region is said to continue today. No dated present-day source was found for it. The tree has no Kongo entry after 1650.
wanted: A dated statement from a Catholic diocese of Mbanza Congo, Matadi or Boma, or a dated study of Kongo Christians after 1650.
openQuestion: No dated source was found that links today's Kongo-region dioceses to the church of Afonso I.

presentBody: Japan's Catholic Church and the Hidden Christian communities
descentBasis: The tree grades the link to the Christians who came forward in 1865 as thin. No text from inside the community covers 1650 to 1865.
basis: The tradition reaches today through Japanese Christianity after 1906. The entry's own text says the hidden Christians kept a faith handed down for about 250 years. The tree rates that link thin, because no text from inside the community covers the gap.

The tradition reaches today through the entry on Chinese Catholicism after 1906. The Catholic church in China grew out of this mission. The tree has no entry for Chinese Catholics between 1650 and 1906.

presentBody: Unitarian Church of Transylvania (Hungarian Unitarian Church)
namedGap: the Unitarian church of Transylvania after 1650
basis: The entry's own text says the church in Transylvania still exists as the Hungarian Unitarian Church. No dated present-day source was verified. The tree has no entry for it after 1650.
wanted: A dated report of the Unitarian Church of Transylvania, or the 2021 Romanian national count of Unitarians.
openQuestion: The Polish Brethren wing of this entry did not continue; only the Transylvanian church is alive.

basis: The entry's own text says a small Schwenkfelder Church still exists in Pennsylvania. No dated present-day source was verified. The tree has no Schwenkfelder entry after 1650.
wanted: A dated statement of the Schwenkfelder Church, or a dated edition of the Yearbook of American and Canadian Churches.

tradition: Family of Love and the Spiritualists
basis: Its carriers ended. The entry's own text says neither group lasted as an institution. Franck's writings were read later, but no community continued.
endQuote: Neither group lasted as an institution.

presentBody: Malankara Orthodox, Jacobite, Mar Thoma and Syro-Malabar churches
basis: The tradition reaches today through the Malankara churches and the Mar Thoma Church. The entry's own text says the split of 1653 is still the shape of Christianity in Kerala. The Syro-Malabar Catholic Church also descends from it, and the tree has no entry for that church.

evidence.title: Religiosity, trust in the Church, confessional division and inter-church relations in Ukrainian society (October 2024)
evidence.quote: Members of religious communities who identified themselves with OCU make up 11% of all respondents (in 2021 — 6%)

descentBasis: Two Orthodox bodies in Ukraine both claim the Kyiv Metropolia of Mohyla. The Ecumenical Patriarchate recognised the Orthodox Church of Ukraine in 2019; the other body remains tied to Moscow.
basis: Orthodoxy in Kyiv is alive today. The Orthodox Church of Ukraine published decisions of its Bishops' Council in 2026. A Razumkov Centre survey of 2024 counted its members. The Kyiv Mohyla Academy, which the entry names, reopened in 1991. The tree has no entry for Ukrainian Orthodoxy after 1700.
openQuestion: Two Orthodox bodies in Ukraine both claim this Kyiv heritage, so the present body is disputed.

descentBasis: The Unity was suppressed in 1627, and the entry's own text says a remnant survived underground until 1722. The Moravian Church claims descent, and the 1735 consecration by the Unity's last bishop supports it.
basis: The Unity of the Brethren wing reaches today through the Moravian Church. The entry's own text says a remnant survived underground and found refuge at Herrnhut in 1722. The Utraquist wing ended after 1627. The Moravian entry carries the tradition.
openQuestion: The entry is flagged not living, but its Unity of the Brethren wing continues through the Moravian Church; the Utraquist wing ended.

basis: The Ethiopian church reaches today through the entry on modern Ethiopian and Eritrean Christianity. The entry's own text says the church survives as one of the largest Oriental Orthodox churches.

evidence.quote: The Remonstrant Church is a small Dutch, liberal protestant denomination.

basis: The Remonstrant Brotherhood is alive today. It published its yearly theme for 2026 to 2027 on its own site. A Leiden thesis of 2017 calls it a small Dutch denomination. The Canons of Dort side is carried by the Reformed churches. The tree has no Remonstrant entry after 1650.

evidence.quote: The statistics give a summary of the Church of Norway activity in parishes/municipalities.

evidence.quote: representatives of the approximately four thousand brothers who form part of your Order

basis: The Discalced Carmelites are alive today. The Order's General Definitory wrote a letter to the whole Order in December 2025. An address of September 2021 counts about four thousand friars. The tree has no Carmelite entry after 1622.

namedGap: the church in New France after 1650
descentBasis: The tree's last word is the move of about three hundred Huron Christians to Quebec in 1650. No text in the tree traces a church from them after that year.
basis: The entry's own text stops at 1650 and does not say whether the church continued. No dated present-day source was verified. The tree has no entry for it after 1650.

presentBody: Hutterian Brethren colonies in Canada and the United States

evidence.title: Census documents growth of Hutterite population, colonies
evidence.quote: reveals a population of 58,392 in 544 colonies in North America, almost 3 out of 4 in Canada

basis: The Hutterite Brethren are alive today. A study by the Young Center, reported in 2026, counted 544 colonies in North America. It drew on a directory the Hutterites published in 2024. The tree has no Hutterite entry after 1785.
wanted: A dated edition of the Hutterite-published directory or a dated statement of the Brethren.
